name: Andrew R J Bonfield
current_role: CFO Emeritus / retired CFO, Caterpillar Inc. (advisory role May-Oct 2026); Senior Independent Non-Executive Director, Reckitt
profile: South African-trained chartered accountant who became one of the most experienced big-company CFOs: SmithKline Beecham, BG Group, Bristol-Myers Squibb (2002-08), National Grid (2010-18) and Caterpillar (2018-26), where he was the first CFO hired from outside. He handed over to Kyle Epley in May 2026 and retires Oct 1, 2026.
interesting_fact: Named 2025 CFO of the Year by the CFO Leadership Council and Chief Executive Group; he was Caterpillar's first externally hired CFO after a long insider tradition.
deep_cut_fact: After joining Caterpillar he trained at its Peoria demonstration and learning center, driving an articulated truck and operating an excavator: 'The best way to learn the iron is to get on it.' He earned his BCom at the University of Natal in Durban.
notes: Ex-National Grid CFO, so the energy/utility angle is relevant. Caterpillar press releases list enterprise media contacts, but the pages blocked fetching so I couldn't verify them; use the caterpillar.com newsroom. Now leaving executive life, so he may have more time.

name: Joseph M Hogan
current_role: President and CEO, Align Technology (Invisalign, iTero), since June 2015
profile: Industrial and medtech executive who spent 25+ years at GE, including 8 years as CEO of GE Healthcare, then ran Swiss power and automation group ABB (2008-13) before taking over Align Technology, maker of Invisalign clear aligners and iTero scanners, in 2015. His wealth comes mainly from Align equity.
interesting_fact: Before dental aligners he ran ABB, a ~$40B power-grid and automation company, so he has led both a grid/electrification giant and a consumer-medical-device firm. Align says he grew GE Healthcare revenue from $7B to $16B.
deep_cut_fact: He didn't come from an elite school: his B.S. in business and economics is from Geneva College, a small Christian college in Beaver Falls, Pennsylvania, and his MBA is from Robert Morris University near Pittsburgh.
notes: His ABB years (power grids, electrification) are the natural angle for an energy podcast. Go through Align corporate communications.

name: Steven J. Fasching
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Deckers Brands (UGG, HOKA); Director, Nature's Sunshine Products
profile: Finance executive and CFO of Deckers Brands since June 2018. He joined Deckers in 2011 to run strategic financial planning, then led strategy and investor relations, and became CFO during HOKA's rapid growth. His wealth comes from Deckers equity. He also sits on the Nature's Sunshine Products board.
interesting_fact: He ran Deckers' investor relations and corporate strategy before becoming CFO, so he has been the company's main voice to Wall Street through the HOKA running-shoe boom.
deep_cut_fact: Before footwear he spent about 20 years at Princess Cruise Lines (Carnival), joining in September 1990 and rising through finance roles to director of finance and assistant controller. He holds a B.S. from Pepperdine and an MBA from UCLA Anderson.
notes: Low public profile outside earnings calls. Best route is Deckers investor relations.

name: Catherine Eva Spear
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and board member, FIGS, Inc. (healthcare apparel)
profile: Catherine 'Trina' Spear co-founded FIGS, a direct-to-consumer maker of medical scrubs, with Heather Hasson in 2013. She left a finance career at Citigroup and then Blackstone (after a Harvard MBA) to do it. She took FIGS public on the NYSE in 2021 and runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: FIGS started with the co-founders selling scrubs out of Hasson's car in hospital parking lots at the 7am/7pm shift changes. Spear recalled 'swiping credit cards on the side of a road outside of an emergency room.'
deep_cut_fact: She liquidated her 401(k) to fund FIGS's first production run, which came back with mislabeled inseams that cost the company $100,000. She moved from New York to LA in January 2013, about seven months after her first call with Hasson.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: Invest Like the Best (Colossus)

notes: Goes by Trina Spear. Media-friendly: many podcast and interview appearances (Invest Like the Best, ICE 'Inside the ICE House', LEADERS magazine).

name: John G Mayer
current_role: Retired; former independent director of TTM Technologies (Sept 2000 to May 7, 2026, retired at the mandatory age of 75)
profile: Veteran printed-circuit-board executive. He was president of Electro-Etch Circuits (1986-94), COO of its successor ElectroStar (1994-96) and VP of Tyco Printed Circuit Group (1997-99), and he joined the board of PCB maker TTM Technologies in 2000. His wealth comes from that PCB lineage and long-held TTM stock. He left TTM's board in May 2026 after 26 years.
interesting_fact: He was a Yale history/arts-and-letters graduate with a UCLA law degree who ended up running circuit-board factories. TTM now makes PCBs for data-center, AI and aerospace/defense electronics.
deep_cut_fact: From 2008 to 2017 he served on the board of trustees of the Cottonwood Gulch Foundation, a nonprofit that runs outdoor expeditions and education programs in New Mexico and the American Southwest.
notes: Retired and very low profile; no personal channels found. Board retirement confirmed: https://iconnect007.com/article/148690/ttm-technologies-appoints-two-new-independent-directors/148687/ein . The only published route is TTM investor relations, which may not forward mail now that he has left the board.

name: Alex Norstrom
current_role: Co-CEO, Spotify Technology S.A. (with Gustav Söderström, since Daniel Ek became Executive Chairman)
profile: Swedish executive who has helped build Spotify's business side since 2011. He moved from VP Growth and Subscriptions to Chief Freemium Business Officer, then co-President and Chief Business Officer, and is now co-CEO responsible for business growth, ads and partnerships. He started at JP Morgan in London, founded startups and worked at King before Spotify.
interesting_fact: He is the architect of Spotify's freemium subscription engine. As co-CEO, Söderström owns product while Norström owns the business: subscriptions, ads and partnerships.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was in his mother's Chinese restaurant in Stockholm. Today he is Co-Executive Sponsor of SPACE, Spotify's Asian & Pacific Islander employee group, and he helped create Gold House's 'Gold Beats' playlist.
notes: Very high-profile role; go through the Spotify press team form. Before Spotify he was Chief New Business Officer at King (Candy Crush) and co-founded Emode and Jetbox.

name: Robert Davis Ravnaas
current_role: President and Chief Financial Officer, Kimbell Royalty Partners (general partner), Fort Worth
profile: R. Davis Ravnaas co-founded the predecessor of Kimbell Royalty Partners in 2013 and has been President and CFO since 2015. Kimbell is an NYSE-listed oil and gas mineral and royalty aggregator, and his father Robert Ravnaas is chairman and CEO. Before Kimbell he was a private-equity associate at Crestview Partners covering energy and industrials. Princeton AB, LSE MSc, Stanford MBA.
interesting_fact: Kimbell doesn't drill. It owns mineral and royalty interests across thousands of US oil and gas wells and collects a cut of production, a 'toll road' model on the US energy supply.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded Kimbell's predecessor in October 2013, while still a student at Stanford GSB (MBA 2014), and served as its VP and CFO from November 2013. Before that, at Crestview Partners (2010-12), he sourced energy and industrials deals.
notes: Goes by Davis Ravnaas. Born ~1986, a young energy CFO and a good fit for an energy podcast. The IR contact is the agency Dennard Lascar (Zach Vaughan).

name: Stacey H Dore
current_role: EVP of Public Affairs and Chief Strategy & Sustainability Officer, Vistra Corp.; independent director, The Williams Companies
profile: Energy lawyer turned executive. After 11 years as a Vinson & Elkins trial lawyer she became EVP and general counsel of Energy Future Holdings (Vistra's predecessor), then general counsel of InfraREIT and CEO of ERCOT utility Sharyland (2019-21). Since 2022 she has been Vistra's first Chief Strategy & Sustainability Officer, overseeing strategy, regulatory and government affairs and communications at one of the largest US power generators, a key supplier of nuclear and gas power to data centers.
interesting_fact: She has spent most of her career inside the Texas power business that became Vistra, from legal team member in 2008 to EVP and general counsel of Energy Future Holdings. She is now Vistra's first-ever Chief Strategy & Sustainability Officer, a role created in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a journalist (BA in journalism, University of Southwestern Louisiana, now UL Lafayette) before Harvard Law, and says she 'chose to be a lawyer because I love to write, and I love to advocate.'
notes: A strong energy/data-center podcast fit: she oversees Vistra's communications function, and she has spoken at conferences such as DistribuTECH (https://www.distributech.com/speakers/stacey-dore). One Vistra hub page lists a different undergraduate school; Dallas Innovates and UT Law say University of Southwestern Louisiana.

name: Ilan Twig
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Navan (formerly TripActions), since 2015
profile: Israeli-born engineer who co-founded TripActions (now Navan), a corporate travel and expense platform, with Ariel Cohen in 2015 and has run its technology ever since. He and Cohen previously co-founded StreamOnce, which Jive Software acquired, and he led engineering at Jive, RockMelt and HP. Navan went public in 2025.
interesting_fact: Skift ranked him No. 2 in its 2026 Power Rankings of the most powerful builders in travel, citing his bet on training Navan's own travel-specific AI models (Navan Cognition and the 'Ava' virtual agent) rather than layering on third-party models.
deep_cut_fact: He and Navan CEO Ariel Cohen are a repeat founding duo: before TripActions they co-founded StreamOnce, acquired by Jive Software, where Twig then served as VP/EVP Engineering (2013-15). He holds a BSc in Computer Science from the Academic College of Tel Aviv-Yaffo.
notes: He writes on the Navan blog. Strong AI-infrastructure angle (Navan trains its own models). Details of the StreamOnce/Jive history come from the Slush bio and other profiles.

name: Ben Nadel
current_role: Web developer, author and podcaster (co-founder and former principal engineer, InVision App); co-host of the Working Code Podcast
profile: Long-time ColdFusion and JavaScript developer who co-founded InVision, the design-prototyping platform once valued at about $2B, and worked there as a principal engineer for years. InVision has since shut down its product. He blogs prolifically at bennadel.com, published the book 'Feature Flags' in 2024 and co-hosts the Working Code Podcast.
interesting_fact: He has run one of the web's longest-lived developer blogs (bennadel.com, once nicknamed 'The Kinky Solutions' blog) for about two decades, publishing several technical posts a week, much of it on ColdFusion.
deep_cut_fact: A QBasic class he took in 1997 made him fall in love with programming. He says 'inspiration is for amateurs' and 'practices' web development at his desk every morning from about 5:30 to 8:30 AM.
notes: Very approachable: his site invites readers to get in touch and to meet up in the New York area. He is a hands-on engineer rather than a business-side founder; a technical/craft angle (feature flags, database performance) would land best. The Hurun '$2B founder' label overstates his business role.

name: Tyler S. Ralston
current_role: Imaging technologist and co-founder of Butterfly Network; his SPIE profile lists him as CTO at ONI (super-resolution microscopy). Current title not confirmed for 2026.
profile: PhD imaging scientist (UIUC Beckman Institute) who worked at MIT Lincoln Laboratory and Lawrence Livermore before co-founding Butterfly Network in 2011 within Jonathan Rothberg's 4Catalyzer incubator. There he led signal processing and imaging for the handheld ultrasound-on-a-chip device. He has since worked on other 4Catalyzer-linked imaging ventures (Hyperfine, Tesseract Health) and is an inventor on dozens of ultrasound patents.
interesting_fact: He was named the first and only '4Catalyzer Fellow' (2015), an honorary title recognizing extraordinary contributions inside Butterfly Network and Rothberg's 4Catalyzer group.
deep_cut_fact: At MIT Lincoln Laboratory (2007-10) he was co-principal investigator on a real-time through-wall radar imager that drew national press. He also built multi-GPU code to propagate satellite orbits for the Space Fence performance-evaluation system.
notes: The email is self-published on his own CV, but the CV is old (circa 2016), so the MIT alias may be stale. Current employer unconfirmed (SPIE profile: CTO at ONI): https://www.spie.org/profile/Tyler-Ralston . A deep-tech scientist rather than a business figure; the Hurun '$1B founder' tag reflects Butterfly's valuation.

name: Amit Gupta
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Yulu (Indian shared electric micromobility); co-founder, InMobi
profile: IIT Kanpur mechanical engineer (2000) and Harvard executive MBA who co-founded InMobi, the mobile-advertising company often called India's first profitable internet unicorn, and helped create its Glance lock-screen platform. He stepped back from InMobi operations in 2017 to found Yulu, which started with shared bicycles and became one of India's largest shared electric-scooter and battery-swapping networks. He is also an angel investor in 40+ startups.
interesting_fact: Yulu began with pedal bikes and pivoted to EVs, found product-market fit with delivery riders during COVID, and built a battery-swapping network (Yuma) with ~99.9% uptime. Gupta wants Yulu to be the 'AWS of mobility.'
deep_cut_fact: IIT Kanpur gave him its Distinguished Alumnus Award in 2013, about 13 years after he graduated with a B.Tech in mechanical engineering, recognizing his entrepreneurship at InMobi.
notes: A very common name: make sure outreach targets the InMobi/Yulu co-founder. Strong EV and battery-swapping energy angle. No published press email found; Yulu's site is JavaScript-only. He writes on YourStory: https://yourstory.com/author/amitgupta-yulu

name: Christian Beedgen
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO, Sumo Logic. His current (2026) role is not confirmed; third-party profiles show his Sumo Logic roles ending in 2023.
profile: Software architect who co-founded Sumo Logic in 2010 and as CTO built its multi-tenant, cloud-native log and machine-data analytics platform, used by 1,600+ customers. Sumo Logic IPO'd in 2020 and was taken private by Francisco Partners in 2023. Before Sumo he was an early engineer, engineering director and chief architect at security company ArcSight.
interesting_fact: Sumo Logic was among the first log-analytics platforms designed as multi-tenant SaaS from day one, rather than software customers ran themselves, a bet he made in 2010 after a decade building on-premise log tools at ArcSight.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sumo Logic he was one of ArcSight's early engineers and became chief architect of its event-based products, ArcSight ESM and ArcSight Logger, the SIEM and log-management tools that Sumo's cloud approach later challenged.
notes: Low public profile since Sumo Logic went private in 2023. MarketScreener lists a 'Gigaton, Inc.' founder role, but I could not verify it and it is probably unrelated to the London climate-AI startup Gigaton. Check his LinkedIn for his current venture before outreach. No published contact found.

name: Gagan Biyani
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Maven (cohort-based online courses platform)
profile: Fremont-born, Berkeley-educated serial founder. He co-founded Udemy in 2009 (now a public online-learning company), was a growth advisor at Lyft, started the Growth Hackers Conference, and co-founded food-delivery startup Sprig (raised $57M; closed 2017). He now runs Maven, a cohort-based course platform he co-founded with altMBA co-creator Wes Kao and Shreyans Bhansali.
interesting_fact: He came up with Sprig, a 15-20-minute healthy-meal delivery startup whose head chef was Google's former executive chef Nate Keller, while advising Lyft. He and co-founder Neeraj Berry made Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before Udemy he was a TechCrunch writer covering mobile apps. He broke the story of a PR firm writing fake App Store reviews, which led to an FTC investigation that quoted his findings.
notes: Very accessible online: active on X and has a personal blog. His site says he lives in Oakland and serves as interim Director of Empower Oakland in his spare time. Ex-journalist, so he may respond well to a well-crafted note.
